extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, copyeditors, indexers, publishers, and librarians producing and preparing books and articles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing, editing, and indexing scholarly and general publications (bibliographies, citations, abbreviations, indexes, punctuation, accessibility, and ancillary materials). Intended to guide layout, citation practice, and editorial decisions for books, journals, and reference works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and uses of abbreviations and their behavior in text, lists, tables, and notes (when to spell out vs. abbreviate, punctuation, capitalization, plural and possessive forms, and indexing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers alphabetizing of abbreviations; use with articles (a or an); treatment in chart labels and compound terms; when to spell out on first occurrence and when to repeat after long intervals; treatment in tables and notes; typographic considerations (italic vs. roman, small caps vs. lowercase, spacing); word division and line breaks; and marking manuscripts or proofs for spelled-out forms. Cross-references: see acronyms; abbreviations specific entries (Bible, journal titles, dates, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations — specific categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for particular classes of abbreviations (Bible, business/commerce, eras, geographic/postal, journal titles, mathematical, musical works, personal and organization names, Latin abbreviations, time designations, and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives sectioned guidance for how to treat different kinds of abbreviations in citations, indexing, and text (e.g., Bible citations, journal titles, postal codes, Latin abbreviations like et al., and mathematical abbreviations). Advises on punctuation, capitalization, indexing, and when to use spelled-out forms for each category; cross-references numerous paragraph numbers for exact examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acronyms and initialisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for formation, capitalization, spacing, and use of acronyms and initialisms in running text, charts, indexes, and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on acronyms as adjectives, capitalization norms, when to omit spaces, small vs. full-size capitals, treatment in journal titles and indexes, and use with articles. See also abbreviations general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetizing and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and rules for alphabetizing bibliographies and indexes, including letter-by-letter vs. word-by-word ordering, treatment of articles, compound terms, non-English names, names with particles, numerals, punctuation, and publisher or author preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies basic rule for indexing; that articles are often disregarded in alphabetizing; use of letter-by-letter preferred; handling of compound terms and subentries; computerized sorting and dedicated indexing software; alphabetical treatment of contributors lists and frequently cited works; handling of non-English personal names and place-names; punctuation and special-character considerations; guidance on checking and quality control for indexes (e.g., cross-references, software checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access dates in citations
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to include access dates for online resources and databases in source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates generally to include access dates for websites/webpages, maps, databases, scientific databases, and some reference works; cross-references rules for author-date systems and specific citation formats (journal articles, reference works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of content (alt text, tables, TTS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to ensure accessibility of illustrations, tables, and electronic content for readers with disabilities and for assistive technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for alternative text for illustrations, accessible tables and multimedia, resources and tool guidance for accessibility, use of text-to-speech tools, and consideration of accessibility in file formats and electronic publications. Cross-references relevant sections for markup and alternative-text standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments — content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include in acknowledgments and where to place them in books and articles (format of term, placement in book, permissions, and illustration credits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies placement (copyright page, separate section, table notes), what material is appropriate (grants, subventions, data-source acknowledgments, illustration credits), omission from indexing, relationship to permissions, and guidance on submitting acknowledgments in manuscripts and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts — preparation and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for preparing abstracts for books, dissertations, theses, and journal articles, including provenance, proofreading, metadata, and relation to copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers abstracts of books, journal articles, and dissertations; links between abstracts and metadata; proofreading and manuscript-preparation guidance; source citation treatment for abstracts; and handling of abstracts with respect to copyright and access rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active vs. passive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference and guidance on use of active voice in prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of active voice and references multiple sections where active voice is recommended (with paragraph citations). Advises on clarity and stronger prose using active constructions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampersand (&) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using ampersands in names, titles, citations, and running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers alphabetizing with ampersands, use in company and publisher names, spacing conventions, omission of the serial comma before an ampersand in some styles, use in legal-style citations, initialisms with ampersands, ampersands in URLs and email addresses, and display in titles of works. Advises following legal or publisher-specific citation instructions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostrophe usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming possessives, plurals in special cases, contractions, and punctuation with apostrophes across languages and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains general possessive rules (attributive nouns, compounds, joint possessives, nouns plural in form but singular in meaning), punctuation interactions, marking in manuscripts/proofs, uses in abbreviated decades and years, differences vs. prime symbol, handling in non-English languages, and inappropriate uses to avoid. Cross-references to legal citations and other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses — email and mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of email addresses and mailing addresses in text and citations, including punctuation, line breaks, abbreviations, and whether to include in source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides on hyperlinks to email addresses, line-break rules, punctuation around email addresses, omission rules in formal citations, abbreviations used in mailing addresses (states, compass points), numbers in addresses, publishers’ addresses in citations, and formatting within running text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendixes (appendices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing appendixes: content, numbering, placement, submission, indexing, and treatment as electronic supplementary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on chronologies and discographies as appendixes; numbering and formatting of figures and notes in appendixes; placement in book and table of contents; running heads; indexing and submission guidelines; using appendixes as electronic supplementary material; and permissions/copyright considerations for appendix material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity of research subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to protect anonymity of research subjects in published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes anonymity of research subjects as a concern and links to sections on interviews, personal communications, and ethics in textual treatment. Advises redaction or anonymization where appropriate and cites relevant paragraphs for detailed handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotations (notes and keyed annotations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of annotations and keyed notes (format, placement, and use in electronic files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers annotations as potentially copyrightable, keying to line or page numbers, use of annotations in PDFs, and relation to endnotes/footnotes. Advises consistent formatting and correct keying in proofs and final files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthologies — editorial and copyright treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial handling of anthologies, including permissions, bracketed editorial additions, source notes, and copyright issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains anthologies as collective works with permissions and rights considerations; editorial additions should be bracketed; material copyrightability within anthologies; permissions and fees; treatment of unnumbered source notes; and guidance on compiling previously published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment in layout and mathematical material
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for alignment of facing pages, tables (cell alignment, decimal points), mathematical expressions, and outlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules for alignment of facing pages and running heads, marking alignment on manuscript and proofs, alignment of table cells and decimal points, alignment in mathematical expressions and equations (with paragraph/figure references), and alignment conventions in outlines and poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotations and editorial alterations in manuscript/proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: How to mark and handle author’s, editor’s, and designer’s alterations and corrections in manuscripts and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines author’s alterations (AAs), editor’s (EAs), and designer’s (DAs); guidance for marking additions and insertions, corrections, setting or reversal of changes, relation to proofreading, and how to indicate these on manuscripts and proofs (with figure/paragraph references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access rights and open-access publishing models
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of access rights and open-access models when preparing or citing materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes access rights relation to abstracts and databases, open-access publishing models, and implications for metadata, permissions, and how materials are cited or made available. Cross-references sections on copyright and permission handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization, typography, and special-character treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for capitalization (titles, acronyms), typographic choices (italic vs. roman, small caps), treatment of special characters, and modernizing archaic letters or non-Latin scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses typographic decisions for abbreviations and acronyms, italicization of titles, small-cap use, spacing conventions, handling of special characters in indexing and electronic files, modernization of archaic letters, and Unicode/technical standards references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and punctuation of names and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for personal names (including non-English forms), organization names, titles of works, and how these affect citations and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains rules on personal-name ordering, particles (Mac, Mc, O’), initials, names with numbers, treatment of titles and offices as appositives, punctuation with names, and how to treat titles of works (italics for full titles, vs. short titles) in source citations and indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation, compound modifiers, and adjective/adverb rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on hyphenation of compound modifiers, adjective and adverb formation, and related punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers hyphenation rules for age terms, compound modifiers and participial adjectives, placement of adjectives (attributive vs predicate), hyphenation in noun compounds, punctuation when adjectives are appositives, comparative and superlative forms, and cross-references to sections on numbers and units of measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-citation conventions for legal and public documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Special citation rules for acts, treaties, legal-style citations, and government publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies treatments in source citations for acts and treaties, legal-style citation formats and particulars (including ampersand and apostrophe usage in such citations), and references to specialized guides like ALWD and other legal-citation resources.
